title: In situ detection of the eIF4F translation initiation complex in mammalian cells and tissues
protocol: Place 12 mm cover glass in a 100 mm glass petri dish.
Autoclave the placed cover glass.
Dry the autoclaved cover glass at 37°C in a heating oven for 16-24 hours.
Place two sterile 12 mm cover glass in each well of a six-well culture plate.
Plate 2 × 10^5 cells per well in 2 mL of culture medium.
Perform serial dilution of cell numbers to determine optimal number for different cell lines, if necessary.
Leave the newly plated cells under the hood for 5 minutes with minimal vibrations.
Incubate cells for 24 hours at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Mix the cells in each well to ensure there are no obvious cell aggregates present in the suspension.
Check the suspended cells before incubation at 37°C to confirm they are homogeneously distributed in each well.
Do not further shake the plate until the cells attach.
After 24 hours of growth, check again under microscope to ensure that cell distribution is homogeneous and no obvious cell clusters are present in each well.
Remove the cover glass from the culture medium using an "L" shape needle made from an insulin syringe.
Take the cover glass gently with surgical forceps to avoid breaking it.
Dry the cover glass on a piece of paper by touching its edge lightly.
Prepare a slide covered with parafilm and place it in a 10 mm petri dish.
Place the cover glass on the pre-prepared parafilm.
Pipette 30 μL of 4% PFA onto the cover glass under a chemical hood.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Prepare a 24-well plate by adding 1.5 mL of 1× PBS to each well.
Recover the cover glass on a filter paper.
Remove the 4% PFA solution by touching the edge of the cover glass on a filter paper.
Draw a circle with an Immedge hydrophobic barrier pen around the cover glass.
Place the cover glass in a prepared 24-well plate filled with 1.5 mL 1× PBS for 5 min at room temperature.
Gently remove the PBS solution with a vacuum pump.
Add 30 μL of 1× PBS Tween-20 0.2% solution for 10 min at room temperature.
Add 1.5 mL of a 1× PBS solution in each well without removing the 1× PBS Tween-20 0.2% solution and incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Gently remove the 1× PBS solution with a vacuum pump.
Add 30 μL of the Blocking Solution on each cover glass.
Incubate for 20 min at 37°C.
Pause Point: The cover glass with the blocking solution can be stored overnight at 4°C.
Dilute eIF4E (anti-mouse) and eIF4G (anti-rabbit) antibodies 1:500 in the antibody diluent to detect the eIF4E-eIF4G interaction.
Alternatively, dilute eIF4E (anti-mouse) and 4EBP1 (anti-rabbit) antibodies 1:500 in the antibody diluent to detect the eIF4E-4EBP1 interaction.
Add a solution of 1× PBS in each well without removing the blocking solution and gently/immediately aspirate with vacuum pump.
Incubate primary antibody solution on the cover glass for 1 h at 37°C.
Do not allow the sample to dry.
Fill non-used wells within the 24-well plate with a solution of 1× PBS.
Add 1.5 mL of Wash Buffer A in each well.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed (64 rpm).
Remove the wash buffer with vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Dilute Mouse Plus and Rabbit Minus PLA probes stock solutions in antibody diluent to 1:5.
Add 30 μL of the PLA probes mixed solution on the cover glass.
Incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Add 1.5 mL of Wash Buffer A in each well after incubation.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed (64 rpm).
Remove the wash buffer with vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Prepare the ligation reaction solution at room temperature as needed for the next step.
Gently remove the wash buffer A with a vacuum pump after the second time of previous step.
Add 30 μL of the ligation reaction mix on the cover glass.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Add 1.5 mL of Wash Buffer A to each well.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed (64 rpm).
Remove the wash buffer with a vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Prepare the rolling cycle amplification solution at room temperature, protected from light.
Gently remove the wash buffer A with a vacuum pump after the second wash.
Add 30 μL of the amplification reaction mix on the cover glass.
Incubate for 1.5 h at 37°C in the dark.
Add 1.5 mL of Wash Buffer B to each well.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed (64 rpm).
Remove the wash buffer with a vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Gently remove the wash buffer B with a vacuum pump.
Add 1 mL of 1:100 diluted Wash Buffer B in high purity water.
Wash samples with 1:100 diluted wash buffer B at least once before performing immunostaining.
Perform routine immunofluorescence or probe-based methods for further processing of the samples.
Air-dry cover glass on paper filter during 15 min.
Add 2 μL of mounting medium with DAPI to each cover glass.
Mount cover glass onto a microscopic slide gently pressing with a syringe rubber.
Seal mounted slides with nail polish if using regular mounting media.
Avoid producing air bubbles in the process of mounting the cover glass.
Store sealed slides at 4°C before microscopy image acquisition.
Do not freeze the slide.
Mount the slide onto the microscope stage for automated scanning.
Open the Control system VS-ASWFL on the computer.
Select “Fluorescence Batch” button in the window of Batch Scan.
The microscope will automatically scan the total number and positions of the slides.
Set up acquisition of z stacks, covering the thickness of the cells in an optimal way.
Acquire 3 levels of z stack with 1 μm each for quantification of relative number of translation initiation complex.
Acquire −1 μm and +1 μm corresponding to the auto-focus plane for relative number of translation initiation complex.
Acquire 20 z-stacks at each selected xy position in each wavelength channel with oil-immersion 63× objective for absolute number of translation initiation complex.
Start acquisition with Cy5, then DAPI for absolute number of translation initiation complex.
Adjust illumination times for each slide to obtain optimal resolutions.
Avoid excessive exposure time to prevent saturation of pixel intensities.
Acquire overview of the slide with 4× objective in DAPI channel with 150 ms exposure time.
Select at least 3 scan positions on each cover glass of the slide.
Process image acquisition with 20× objective and mirror cube QUAD, starting with DAPI channel (450 nm) with 3 ms exposure time.
Capture Cy5 channel (644 nm/670 nm) with 300 ms exposure time at 3 z stack planes.
Export images acquired by Olympus Virtual Slide scanner from VSI format using the BIOP-tool plugin in ImageJ.
Open TIFF images saved from TCS SPE Leica confocal microscope in ImageJ as sequential images.
Save stacks of images in DAPI and Cy5 channels as TIFF format.
Open TIFF images in ImageJ software.
Select Process/Binary/MakeBinary in the main menu of ImageJ.
Select Process/Filter/Median 2.0 in the main menu of ImageJ.
Select Process/Binary/Watershed in the main menu to segment spots.
Select Process/Binary/Find_Maxima in the main menu to exclude edge maxima, light background.
Use FISH-Quant software for 3-dimension quantification of spots.
